problem: Existing POI-goal navigation benchmarks are either coarse (street-segment level, graph-based like CitySeeker) or open-loop on AI-generated videos (BridgeNav, ABot-N0), so they cannot test closed-loop, entrance-level 'final-meters' arrival in realistic scenes. Prior POI methods also collapse targets to pixel goals and use heavy task-specific architectures.
motivation: Real-world navigation is POI-driven, and reaching the exact entrance of a POI is the decisive last step for deploying robots in human-centric environments. Open-loop scores on generated video mostly measure imitation of the training distribution, not interactive navigation ability. Scaling continuous trajectory data is hard, so the authors scale semantic grounding instead.
key_idea: Decouple POI navigation into a VLM Brain that grounds signage then entrance boxes (used as cropped visual cues) and an Action module with elastic temporal sampling and latent queries that regresses continuous waypoints, evaluated on a new closed-loop 3DGS Isaac Sim benchmark.
insight: The grounding stage is the upper bound: the fine-tuned brain reaches 98.8% referential correctness vs 91.6% for the backbone VLM, and POINav beats OmniNav (42.33 vs 34.36 SR 2m) under the same action training data. Failure analysis shows the remaining errors come from the action policy trained on BridgeNav (generated videos), which lacks large heading offsets, not from grounding. Note that no ablation isolates elastic sampling or the adaptive crop.
method: POINav-Bench: 11 commercial areas reconstructed with LiDAR+photogrammetry into 3DGS (126,398 m², 163 POIs), run in Isaac Sim with collision meshes; entrances annotated as horizontal boxes; start points sampled on walkable regions; A* GT trajectories from MoGe-V2 normals.
Semantic-to-Geometric POI grounding: Brain (VLM) factorizes P(b_id|V,L)·P(b_geo|b_id,V,L), first localizing the signage box and then the entrance box conditioned on it.
Adaptive viewpoint cue: the crop C_t is the entrance box if visible, otherwise the signage box, giving the action model an image-goal-like visual reference as signage leaves the FOV.
Elastic Temporal Sampling: keeps K uniformly time-dilated frames over the whole history plus the current frame, giving global context at constant cost.
Latent Action Querying: a Qwen2.5-VL-3B backbone encodes the frames and cue; learnable queries cross-attend to the latents and an MLP decodes future waypoints (no diffusion).

POINav-Dataset pipeline: automated curation of 70K signage–entrance pairs from street-view sequences using frame filtering, VLM entrance prediction, rule-based validation and a straight-line traversability check.

setting.backbone: Qwen2.5-VL-3B (fine-tuned) for both Brain and Action modules, with cross-attention latent queries and an MLP head
setting.training_data: Brain: POINav-Dataset with 70K real-world signage-entrance pairs. Action: BridgeNav dataset (trajectories from Wan2.1-I2V generated videos).
setting.observation: egocentric monocular RGB with history frames

numbers.extra: Action module trained on BridgeNav dataset; brain trained on POINav-Dataset; start >10 m from target POI; SR uses 2 m threshold

numbers_note: Only one result table on the new benchmark (no official split names; 'test' is an assumption). Grounding metrics (RC 98.8%, GQ 94.8%) are on hundreds of samples and are not navigation numbers.
results: On POINav-Bench, POINav gets 42.33 SR(2m) and 40.29 SPL, beating OmniNav trained on BridgeNav (34.36/31.52), untrained vanilla OmniNav (23.92/22.44) and ViNT (19.01/18.24). The brain module reaches 98.8% referential correctness and 94.8% grounding quality vs 91.6%/88.0% for the backbone VLM.
limitations: Only 11 commercial areas in simulation, so limited diversity and sim-to-real gap not addressed; no real-robot tests.
Action policy trained on generated BridgeNav videos lacks large heading offsets, so it fails with large initial angular offsets and multiple visible POIs.
Baselines are few and there are no ablations of the framework components; entrance ambiguity with multi-entrance buildings and unclear signage remains.
